subthemes.name: Learning from human guidance and feedback
subthemes.gist: Teaching agents by showing them examples of good behavior or asking them to prefer one action over another, without needing to specify rewards.

subthemes.name: Making language models and reasoning better with reinforcement learning
subthemes.gist: Using reinforcement learning techniques to help large language models reason through problems step-by-step, improve their reasoning chains, or align their outputs with human preferences.

subthemes.name: Building and using learned world models
subthemes.gist: Training agents to learn a model of how the world works, then using that model to plan actions or simulate outcomes without constantly trying things in the real world.

subthemes.name: Coordinating multiple agents together
subthemes.gist: Teaching groups of agents to work together, communicate, or compete, where each agent learns how to interact with the others and adapt to their behavior.

subthemes.name: Exploring efficiently and avoiding costly mistakes
subthemes.gist: Finding smart ways to explore unknown situations without wasting time, and understanding how much the agent could regret a bad decision so we know when to stop exploring.

subthemes.name: Making agents robust and safe in real scenarios
subthemes.gist: Building agents that don't break when conditions change, can recover from adversarial situations, and avoid catastrophic failures even when faced with surprising or hostile inputs.

subthemes.name: Learning well from limited or offline data
subthemes.gist: Training agents effectively using only recorded data without interaction, or learning efficiently from a small amount of experience, which is crucial when real-world trials are expensive.

subthemes.name: Breaking down complex goals into simpler steps
subthemes.gist: Teaching agents to break large tasks into smaller subgoals or skills, and learning when and how to use each skill, so they can handle long-term, multi-step problems.
